doc.title: Sherrie Maricle interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Drummers she tells students to hear
summary: Her heroes include Mel Lewis, Buddy Rich, Jeff Hamilton, Dennis Mackrel, Jo Jones, Philly Joe Jones and Elvin Jones.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Do you have a list of must-listen-to drummers for young players?

Well, Mel Lewis is one of my absolute idols. I think he swings. Big band drummers I divide into two categories, Mel Lewis for sure and I love Buddy Rich, I always loved Buddy Rich. He’s like one of the, you know you can pick out the geniuses like Oscar Peterson on the piano and Buddy, like people who do, and Art Tatum, people who could play what nobody will ever be able to duplicate what these people have done, and he’s one of those. I love Jeff Hamilton right now who is a drummer in Los Angeles, one of my favorite players. Dennis Mackrel I think is a great drummer. And I love all the Jo Jones and all the great drummers with the Basie bands. I mean I have a really long listening list I make all my students take. And you’ve got to listen to — go find one of these records. And for small group playing I love Philly Joe Jones, he’s probably one of my favorite players. Yeah. And Elvin Jones. I just — the list is endless.
